purpose: Non-admission discovery of independently identified global catastrophe hazard, building exposure, drought context and historical flood-depth products missing from the existing source registry; access, data rights and scientific fitness remain unapproved.

entries.name: JRC satellite-derived flood depth maps for Europe
entries.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre / CEMS
entries.spatial_scope: Europe; satellite-observed flood events where acquisitions exist
entries.temporal_scope: 2015-2024 in the currently catalogued JRC dataset; archive may subsequently expand
entries.resolution_or_granularity: 20 m flood-depth GeoTIFFs; event-start and event-end in filename; centimetres; 9999 denotes permanent or seasonal water bodies
entries.note: Separate JRC depth reconstruction product from the already registered CEMS GFM v4.1.1 flood-extent monitoring. Depth is model-assisted reconstruction from Sentinel-1 extent and topography, not a gauge-measured depth or insured loss. Preserve event ID/date, acquisition coverage, raster CRS, cm units, dummy 9999 water-body mask and spatial validity. The third-party EuroFlood index advertises an extended 2015-2025 range: independently verify its exact catalogue vintage and lineage before joining. Never count GFM and these derived depths as independent observations.

entries.name: OpenBuildingMap global footprints and estimated building attributes
entries.spatial_scope: Global, according to coverage of its three input footprint families
entries.temporal_scope: 2025 publication; source snapshots include OSM July 2024, Google Open Buildings and Microsoft building footprints
entries.resolution_or_granularity: About 2.7 billion footprint polygons with inferred occupancy, height and floorspace, distributed as tiled building records
entries.note: Original providers include OSM, Google Open Buildings and Microsoft, which are already known separately; this derived product does not add an independent building population or measured attributes. Height uses GHSL; occupancy draws on OSM land use/POI, and floorspace is derived. Preserve original footprint family, dedup/conflation, tile and release identity. Dataset states ODbL 1.0; assess share-alike and commercial redistribution obligations for exact use; no insured values or vulnerability functions.

entries.name: WRI Aqueduct Floods Hazard Maps Version 2
entries.spatial_scope: Global coverage subject to flood-model spatial limits
entries.temporal_scope: Historical/baseline and projections for 2030, 2050 and 2080; version 2 corrected 2020-10-20
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Single-band GeoTIFF inundation depth in metres; riverine/coastal, return period, climate scenario and coastal subsidence options vary by file
entries.note: This is Aqueduct Floods v2, not the separate Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk Atlas. Provider warns the 2020 model omits flood protections; historical and future scenarios are modelled not observed. A 2020-10-20 river-map bias correction requires exact corrected asset identity, return-period/scenario/subsidence flag, datum, grid and hash. Do not treat a return-period surface as an event catalogue, or sum it with JRC floods as independent losses.

entries.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 global water-risk indicators
entries.spatial_scope: Global basins and reported country/provincial aggregates
entries.temporal_scope: Current baseline and projections to 2030, 2050 and 2080; Aqueduct 4.0 documentation
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Basin-level baseline annual/monthly and future water-risk indicators; aggregated rankings and multiple component metrics
entries.note: Not the Aqueduct Floods v2 depth maps and not an annual stochastic drought loss event set. Indicators combine heterogeneous inputs; aggregate rankings are lossy and not measured site-level hazard or insurer exposure. Preserve basin-level identifiers, indicator meaning, epoch, climate model, raw component and uncertainty; original WRI CC BY attribution and provider registration/usage instructions require an exact scope review.

entries.name: GEM Global Seismic Hazard Map v2026.1
entries.temporal_scope: Version v2026.1 issued June 2026; supersedes v2023.1
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Base map of PGA in g on reference rock Vs30 800 m/s at 10% exceedance probability in 50 years; vector/raster map products
entries.note: The base map is a composite of regional/national PSHA models and is not an event catalogue or loss model. Exact layer/format licensing differs: public hazard map is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and commercial use requires separate agreement. Preserve PGA units, return/exceedance definition, soil reference, version, composite regional boundaries and model dependencies. Do not assert spatial independence from ESHM20 or translate PGA directly into property claims.

entries.name: Imperial College Storm Model IRIS 10000-year synthetic tropical cyclones
entries.provider: Imperial College London / Sparks and Toumi
entries.spatial_scope: Global tropical cyclone basins represented by input observation period
entries.temporal_scope: 2024 data publication, fixed present-climate representation based on 1980-2021 observations
entries.resolution_or_granularity: 10000-year global synthetic tropical cyclone track/time-step data, distributed by basin in text archives; 3-hour time steps
entries.note: IRIS uses IBTrACS v04r00 and ERA5 fields, both upstream-dependent, so do not treat IRIS versus STORM or IBTrACS as wholly independent evidence. Simulates the post-lifetime-maximum-intensity stage, excludes pre-peak track evolution and extra/post-tropical storms, and years are independent without interannual correlation. Preserve basin/year/event identity and wind averaging definitions before comparing with STORM v4; a synthetic track is not an observed insured loss. Code is GPL-3.0; exact Figshare dataset rights require separate review.
